questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Most crucial to me was the cultural aspect. I've always wanted to experience what it is like to go to college in America and I really wanted to explore the southern part of the country which was where I spent my time abroad.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Getting the full American college experience was maybe one of the best decisions I've ever made. Everything from football, frat parties, college bars and basically living on campus was so much fun. Highly recommend.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find the information I needed to know before arrival. My host institution was incredibly helpful and sent out formulas that needed to be filled out and other information by email so us international students were kept informed. If I had questions or other inquiries we could email the correct department at the host institution which also was really helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't get any assistance when I arrived since everything was handled before arriving.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it really easy to find off campus housing. I would recommend using the housing portal provided by the host institution where students can put their house/partment/room up for rent if they're going abroad themselves. That way you know it is less likely to be a scam since the account is linked to the email adress you get as a student. Otherwise, Facebook groups worked really well for a lot of other internationals.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That there is different areas which depends on what type of vibe you are looking for. One side of the streets right off campus can be a party street with parties being thrown every weekend and tons of nightlife activities, and the other side of the streets can be more of a residential area with a more chill vibe.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The host institution emailed us when it was time to register at the university. The whole registration was very easy since you basically just have to provide them with information you already are in possession of. The whole registration at the host institution took maybe 5 minutes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email the international department if you had any questions. They answered quite quickly and gave helpful advice.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got every class I signed up for. Be sure to register for classes as soon as class registration opens up in order not to be waitlisted an possible miss out on a class.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing really - it is quite self explanatory and easy to do once you have been granted a place at the host institution by UCPH.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The general level seemed to be a bit easier than the one at UCPH. The level of the courses were also incredibly dependent on the individual professor with some being more chill and others being more uptight. However, they all expected that students come prepared for class but it was very different how many questions and the level of questions they would ask. But all classes were very doable by following along in class and reading the material for each class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They used cold calling which is quite a difference from UCPH. Again, the professors would have a different approach to cold calling with some requiring each student to answer at least one question in class and others only picking on volunteers. The teaching style was also way more dependent on student interaction and discussion. Classes were way more engaging if people volunteered and the teaching style was based on student discussion on both cases and hypotheticals.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to the Law of the US, Intellectual Property, Business Enterprises, and Trusts and Estates.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Business Enterprises with professor Batlan was incredibly insightful in regards to US business law. The class covered the different types of companies and also drew upon law from torts. Even as internationals, many of the principles we have learned in a non-common law country was useful so you wouldn't feel lost if you haven't taken common law classes before. The class was primarily based on cases which would be discussed in class. Come prepared to class - otherwise you will not have a good time when being cold called since she was very concerned about the factual circumstances of the cases.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The insurance provided by the school. It is not mandatory but highly encouraged. However, it was very expensive and it is better to be safe than sorry.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Course books were incredibly expensive with some being around $300. Also, food on campus was quite expensive if you were to buy from the shops. You could buy cheaper food other places on campus but it wouldn't be as good.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My host institution is known for being a big party school so there was many frat parties and general parties going on in the weekends. However, you must know somebody in order to get into the frat parties. The university also have a football team which is doing pretty good so going to games on weekends is a must and part of the whole college experience (10/10 fun). The university had a fully equipped gym with basketball courts, swimming pool, weight lifting room, crossfit rooms, squash courts, and everything else a proper gym needs to have which is free to all students. The university would also arrange different "festivals" or get togethers during the semester. You could also join things like the soccer team if you wanted to.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely the college football games. Stand in the student section (which is almost always full) and enjoy the atmosphere and cheap drinks. Pre-game at a day-party at a frat and hit The Boot or Palms after the game = full college experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going out on the weekends and talk to the other American students and other internationals. On holidays (and weekends) I would recommend going on a roadtrip to either Texas or Miami since it is a rather short drive. Otherwise, fly to other places and see other parts of the country while there.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Incredibly easy. The environment is very international-friendly and many of the American students come from other states which makes everybody non-native to the local culture. The local culture was also very easy to adapt to since it is a very friendly place if you don't go the wrong places.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Embrace being international. They love talking to Europeans and many of them have been to Europe themselves on either holiday or exchange. It is a nice ice-breaker and then you can go on from there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That you need a car to basically do anything. Luckily, the off campus housing available is very close to campus (10 minute walk for most) but a car is almost need for everything outside of the campus area (except going downtown with the streetcar). Heavily dependent on Ubers.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How open the locals were. It is very easy making conversation with randoms both when you are on a night out but also just in a restaurant or grocery shopping.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1: Be prepared to be social. You will have a way more fun time if you make decent connections in the first weeks which can lead to other relationships with Americans who can show you the "real" way of going to college. 2: Make an experience of everything. Whether you go to a football game, a rodeo, drinking downtown, or staying on campus, then see the whole thing as an experience. It is so different from Denmark and a major change of scenery which makes you appreciate being in another country and culture way more. Everything is basically entertainment, so be sure to enjoy it. 3: Be aware of your surroundings. It is not as safe as Denmark which the university also emphasizes when there. However, I never saw anything super unsettling or heard anything happen around campus, but it is recommended to stay more alert than back home in Europe.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pack clothes for every season. It can be super hot and humid but also quite cold during winter. Other than that just use your common sense and you'll be more than fine.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Knowing that I can move to a different country, culture, school system and make it work out. Now I know that I'm able to go somewhere I've never been and make incredible memories, meet friends from all over the world, and have the time of my life while also doing a bit of studying.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling like I had to do something every weekend in order to get the most out of my time abroad. I had to remind myself that taking a weekend off to chill by myself was cool which was a little hard if you suffer from FOMO and have many connections with both the Americans and other internationals. However, taking time off was crucial since the whole experience can be somewhat overwhelming if you feel like you have to be out and about during the weekdays and the weekend.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
